listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 543

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Quadr II Praef 9
div.ab: Si qua tamen natiue bonitatis monimenta remanserant, sancxere leges et uiuendi iura, constituerunt urbes et fida receptacula, quo tuta fieret inter improbos innocentia, et, quos ipsa probitatis hórtamenta non excitant, saltem conuertantur ad pene formidinem.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 543 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s print has ‘hórtamenta’ with an acute; transcribed as printed
div.ab: Yet where any monuments of native goodness had remained, they sanctioned laws and rights of living, they founded cities and faithful refuges, whereby innocence might be safe among the wicked, and those whom the very exhortations of probity do not rouse might at least be turned by fear of punishment.
